stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Hydrologists studying forested watersheds in Oregon found that removing streamside trees raised summer water temperatures in narrow headwater creeks by several degrees. Along wide rivers, however, the same kind of clearing produced no measurable warming. The researchers explained that a wide river's surface is mostly exposed to the sun even when its banks are forested, so the trees provide little shade to begin with. If a timber project cleared the trees along both a narrow headwater creek and a wide river, the clearing would most likely ______
choices: raise the water temperature of the headwater creek but not that of the wide river.
raise the water temperature of the wide river but not that of the headwater creek.
lower the water temperature of the headwater creek but not that of the wide river.
raise the water temperatures of the creek and the river by roughly equal amounts.
explanation: Write the finding as one arrow: clearing streamside trees → warmer water → narrow creeks only. Apply it to the new project and you get warming in the creek and no change in the wide river. That is choice A.

B.why: You got the direction right (warming) but swapped the groups. The passage says the wide river showed no measurable warming, and the narrow creek is the one that warmed.

C.why: You got the group right (the creek) but reversed the direction. Taking away shade makes the creek warmer, not cooler.

D.why: You let the effect spread to both water bodies. The passage says clearing had no measurable effect on wide rivers, so equal warming is not supported.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: When a regional insurance company began letting employees work from home three days a week, economist Dana Whitcomb tracked how many workers quit over the next two years. Among employees with commutes longer than an hour, the share who quit fell sharply. Among employees who lived within a short drive of the office, the share who quit hardly changed. Whitcomb's findings suggest that if the company were to end its remote-work policy, ______
choices: employees who live close to the office would likely become more likely to quit.
employees with long commutes would likely become less likely to quit.
employees with long commutes would likely become more likely to quit.
employees across the company would likely quit at much higher rates.
explanation: The arrow is: remote work → fewer quits → long-commute employees only. Ending the policy runs that arrow backward, so quitting should rise among long-commute employees. That is choice C.

A.why: You got the direction right but picked the wrong group. Quit rates for nearby employees hardly changed when the policy started, so you have no reason to expect them to change when it ends.

B.why: You got the group right but kept the original direction. The policy reduced quitting, so taking it away would raise quitting, not lower it.

D.why: You applied the effect to everyone and made it bigger. The study found an effect only among long-commute employees, so a company-wide jump goes beyond the evidence.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Many birdwatchers assume that streetlights make all urban songbirds begin their dawn songs earlier. However, a study of six European species found that the effect depended on eye size. Species with large eyes relative to their bodies, which are more sensitive to dim light, started singing up to forty minutes earlier near streetlights. Species with small eyes sang at the same time whether or not lights were nearby. This suggests that if a town switched off its streetlights at night, ______
choices: small-eyed species there would likely begin singing later than they do now.
large-eyed species there would likely begin singing later than they do now.
large-eyed species there would likely begin singing earlier than they do now.
songbirds of every species there would likely begin singing at a later hour.
explanation: The arrow is: streetlights → earlier singing → large-eyed species only. Remove the lights and the large-eyed species should go back to singing later. That is choice B.

A.why: You got the direction right but chose the wrong group. Small-eyed species were not affected by the lights, so switching the lights off should not change when they sing.

C.why: You got the group right but reversed the direction. The lights moved singing earlier, so removing them should move it later, not even earlier.

D.why: This is the popular view the passage sets out to correct. The study showed that only large-eyed species respond to the lights, so you can't extend the change to every species.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: An adjuvant is an ingredient added to some vaccines to strengthen the immune response. In a recent trial of an influenza vaccine, adding a particular adjuvant greatly increased the number of antibodies produced by adults over sixty-five. In adults under forty, antibody levels were about the same with or without the adjuvant. These results imply that if adults over sixty-five received the vaccine without this adjuvant, they would most likely ______
choices: produce more antibodies than they would if given the adjuvant version.
produce no antibodies at all in response to the influenza vaccine.
produce about as many antibodies as they would with the adjuvant.
produce fewer antibodies than they would if given the adjuvant version.
explanation: The arrow is: adjuvant → more antibodies → adults over sixty-five. Remove the adjuvant for that group and their antibody count should drop compared with the adjuvant version. That is choice D.

A.why: You reversed the direction. For older adults the adjuvant raised antibody levels, so leaving it out should lower them.

B.why: You pushed a reduction all the way to zero. The passage says the adjuvant boosts the response. It never says the vaccine fails without it.

C.why: You applied the younger group's result to the older group. 'About the same' describes adults under forty. For adults over sixty-five, the adjuvant made a large difference.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Astronomers comparing sky surveys taken from rural and suburban sites found that artificial light from nearby towns sharply reduced the number of faint stars visible to the naked eye. The number of bright stars observers could see, by contrast, was nearly identical at both kinds of sites, since those stars outshine the glow of scattered light. Based on these findings, if a suburb sharply dimmed its outdoor lighting, observers there would likely see ______
choices: more bright stars than before, while the number of faint stars stayed about the same.
more faint stars than before, while the number of bright stars stayed about the same.
fewer faint stars than before, while the number of bright stars stayed about the same.
every star in the night sky, including stars only visible through a telescope.
explanation: The arrow is: artificial light → fewer visible stars → faint stars only. Dimming the lights reverses that, so more faint stars appear and the bright-star count stays the same. That is choice B.

A.why: You got the direction right but swapped the groups. Bright stars were visible at both kinds of sites, so dimming the lights changes the faint-star count, not the bright-star count.

C.why: You got the group right but reversed the direction. Light hides faint stars, so less light should reveal more of them, not fewer.

D.why: You stretched 'more faint stars' into 'every star.' The passage covers only stars visible to the naked eye, so telescope-only stars are beyond what it supports.
